fixed.explanation: In non-strict mode the function only rejected trailing digits, so other trailing text such as ' garbage' was accepted. The edit requires any remaining text to be whitespace only, or a 'T' or space separator followed by a digit (the start of a time part, which timestamp parsing needs). Anything else returns an incorrect-format error. I haven't compiled or run this.

query.intent: The date string parser (Date::TryConvertDate) and the cast of VARCHAR to DATE accept trailing characters after a valid date when separated by a space. It should only allow trailing content that is a valid time/timestamp portion (or whitespace), and otherwise fail the conversion.
query.symptom: CAST('2020-01-01 garbage' AS DATE) returns 2020-01-01 instead of throwing a conversion error.

history.analysis: Date::TryConvertDate parses the date and then handles trailing characters. In non-strict mode it appears to accept anything after a space separator. That is why '2020-01-01 garbage' casts to DATE without an error. The fix belongs in the trailing-content handling at the end of this function. TryCast::Operation and TryCastErrorMessage::Operation only call it.
